context.guidance: Serve every route that carries Personal Data over TLS only, and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes on session cookies. Replace wildcard cross-origin rules with an explicit list of trusted origins. These transport and session controls are part of the safeguards Rule 6(1)(a) requires for the Personal Data they carry.

value.fix:
Stop serving Personal Data over plaintext HTTP. In the Terraform config, change the port-80 listener so it only redirects to HTTPS, and add a TLS listener that forwards to the target group:

1. Replace the existing `aws_lb_listener "http"` default_action with a redirect:
```hcl
default_action {
  type = "redirect"
  redirect {
    port        = "443"
    protocol    = "HTTPS"
    status_code = "HTTP_301"
  }
}
```
2. Add an HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate and a modern TLS policy:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.juice_shop.arn
  port              = 443
  protocol          = "HTTPS"
  ssl_policy        =«SECRET»
  certificate_arn   = var.acm_certificate_arn

  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.juice_shop.arn
  }
}
```
3. Set the target group or security group so that no Personal Data route is reachable on port 80.

In the application, also set `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` (or `Lax`) on session cookies, and replace any wildcard CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with an explicit allow-list of trusted origins. These app-level changes are not in the supplied evidence, so they need to be made and verified in the application code separately.
